diagnoses: The reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md does not define concrete deliverable file paths or completion criteria (which files to write under /app/output/, required schema fields, null handling for runs lacking TC data). The 'Output construction guardrails' section mentions rounding/sorting but never names q01.json–q05.json as mandatory outputs, so an agent may skip or misname deliverables.

The Q02 representative-thermocouple selection guidance in reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md is missing/ambiguous. Section 4 'Deterministic sensor selection' only states generic rules ('max metric → smallest tc_id, min metric → smallest tc_id') and the TAL recipe (Section 3) never specifies which TC to pick for TAL. Since TAL compliance is worst-case driven (coolest probe = minimum TAL), the toolkit should explicitly instruct selecting the TC with the minimum TAL (ties by smallest tc_id), consistent with the handbook's worst-case/representative-sensor guidance. Without this, the agent may wrongly reuse Q1's max-ramp TC or pick the maximum TAL.
repair_plan: In reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md, add an explicit 'Deliverables and completion criteria' section listing the five required output files (/app/output/q01.json … q05.json), stating that every run_id in mes_log.csv must appear where required, floats rounded to 2 decimals post-computation, arrays sorted ascending by run_id/board_family/board_id, and null used for genuinely missing data (e.g., runs without TC rows must still appear with null numeric fields and be flagged failing where the question requires it).

In reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md Section 4 (Deterministic sensor selection), add a Q02-specific subsection: for TAL compute per-TC tal_s, then select the representative TC as the worst-case probe = argmin(tal_s) with tie-break by smallest tc_id lexicographically; emphasize this rule may differ from Q01 (max ramp across TCs) and Q03 (min peak), and instruct re-reading the handbook's TAL/representative-sensor section to confirm before applying.
Preserve all existing sorting/dedup, slope, time-above-threshold interpolation, peak/margin, and conveyor feasibility recipes verbatim; only append/clarify the two sections above.
